title: The Emperor sets out for Makka a second time, and leaves early. He stays at court just long enough for his son's wedding to an Ottoman princess, then rides east; the crown prince Ismāʿīl rules as regent. Five years ago the season passed him by in the desert; this time he means to stand at ʿArafāt with time to spare

data.lesson: the game appears to close the Hajj season with the turn of the year; leaving in May allows for pauses on the road
data.regent: the crown prince Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd
data.wedding: the crown prince Ismāʿīl to ʿĀʾisha, an Ottoman princess, just before the Emperor left

title: The crown prince Ismāʿīl takes a second wife, ʿĀʾisha, a princess of the house of ʿOthmān, the rising sultans of Anatolia; his father stays at court for the wedding before setting out on pilgrimage

title: Merchants sent by the Mansa of Mali himself ask to buy the empire's madāfiʿ, the fire-tubes and small bombards of its arsenals, and the craft of casting them. The crown prince Ismāʿīl, ruling as regent, judges it profitable business: Mali pays a fifth of a year's income for the privilege and becomes a grateful friend in western Africa

data.choice: This might be a profitable business
data.rejected: There is no benefit to us to sell guns to them
data.history: not as early as it sounds: the Naṣrids are said to have used gunpowder engines at Huéscar in 1324 and Alicante in 1331, and hand-guns were spreading through the Mediterranean by the 1380s; in the chronicle these are madāfiʿ, fire-tubes, not muskets
data.regent: decided by the crown prince Ismāʿīl as regent, while the Emperor was on the road to Makka (Trent)

title: This time the pilgrimage goes by sea. Off the coast of the Maghrib a merchant ship hails the Emperor's vessels, her decks stacked with silk and fine cloth from distant ports, and the Emperor buys the finest aboard after a merchant's unhurried haggling. The caravan grows more splendid

title: A creature of habit, the Emperor sits again with the scholars of al-Azhar for a month. It was this same pause that cost him ʿArafāt six years ago; this time he arrived in al-Qāhira in July, with five months to spare

data.event: The Royal Ḥajj: The City of a Thousand Minarets

title: The Emperor reaches Makka at last. The Grand Mosque opens before him and the Kaʿba stands at its heart, black-draped and older than memory, with the white-robed faithful circling it from every land where the call to prayer is heard; sultan and shepherd dress alike. Twenty years after he first meant to go, he completes the Hajj, and he distributes gold freely, so that no pilgrim in Makka goes hungry

title: While the Emperor is in Makka, Aiman of the Baḥrī house, his first wife, consort of the empire and sister of the Mamlūk sultan, dies at forty-seven. She had gone home to Miṣr on a visit to her family, and the court's letter says a beast of the Nile took her by the river. Four years after Duʿā, the second of his great wives is gone, and both times the Emperor was far away. Aiman's son Yūsuf, twenty, now has no mother at court. Nobody at court said aloud what some of them thought

data.cause: the game's death notice: attacked by a crocodile
data.whereabouts: not stated; the Emperor was on pilgrimage
data.roles: consort of al-Andalus; mother of Prince Yūsuf, Umm al-Fatḥ and Jadīla bint Saʿd
data.telling: Trent's ruling: the chronicle plants a suspicion and leaves it there. In the story she died on the Nile while visiting her family in Egypt; the game's notice says attacked by a crocodile
